message.abstract: <jats:p>Vietnamese phishing is under-represented in public datasets, and two developments make existingbenchmarks fragile: large language models write fluent lures, and detectors accurate in-distributioncollapse across datasets. We evaluate a multi-channel fusion detector, combining Vietnamese page-text representations (char-n-gram TF-IDF; frozen PhoBERT, PhoBERT-v2, ViSoBERT, XLM-R)with21URL/hostlexicalfeatures.Avariance-correctedevaluationuncoversanobserveddirectionalasymmetry on one cleaned subset: incorporating page-content representations into URL featuresimprovesallfourreportedmetricsforfouroffiveencoders(upto+0.094F1),whereasnostatisticallysignificantincrementalgainfromappendingURLfeaturestocontentembeddingsisresolved(0.54≤𝑞 ≤ 0.95 on F1; 𝑞 ≥ 0.087 on ranking metrics). A seven-fold leave-one-scenario-out test lowersMacro-F1 from 0.928on matched random splits to 0.892, with errors concentrated in benign falsepositives (19.0%). Under a pre-specified token-Jaccard band [0.20,0.30], paraphrasing raises thebaseline miss rate from 3.2%to 17.9%; character-level adversarial training leaves it at 22.8%, whiledisjointparaphraseaugmentationlowersitto5.9%onthiscorpus.Theexplicitleave-one-LLM-outtestis asymmetric: training on Claude rewrites numerically reduces held-out Gemini misses from 23.1%to 17.2%without corrected significance (𝑝 = 0.160), whereas Gemini augmentation increases held-out Claude misses to 36.6%(𝑝<0.001). These results do not establish generator-invariant semanticrobustness; machine-written phishing versus human-written benign controls remains an authorshipconfound.</jats:p>
